title: Wings coach says Paige Bueckers' WNBA Rookie of the Year status is 'clear' - NewsBreak
text: LOS ANGELES — Chris Koclanes made it clear that the 2025 Rookie of the Year award was Paige Bueckers' to lose, especially with her impact in Los Angeles on full display . Despite the Dallas Wings struggling this season, Bueckers has made it clear that she is the top rookie. The star seemingly sets history in just her first year in the league. Additionally, the 23-year-old's penchant for being the leader both on and off the court has paid dividends for a Wings squad looking for a stabilizing presence. And Buecker's impact is not lost on Koclanes, the Wings' head coach. Speaking to reporters before Dallas's 81-80 loss to Los Angeles, the head coach explained how Bueckers is, unequivocally, the Rookie of the Year , especially after the star scored 44 points on 17-of-21 shooting, becoming the first WNBA player in league history to score that much on an 80 percent conversion rate. READ MORE: Fever announce worst possible Sophie Cunningham update and immediately take action READ MORE: Joe Rogan doubles down on conspiracy theory over Donald Trump shooting incident "Yeah, it's just clear — she is rookie of the year. There's no question," Koclanes declared to reporters. "I'm at a loss for words because she's just an incredible talent on and off the floor. So she is our leader and she makes everybody around her better. I mean, you can look at the numbers, the numbers speak for themselves, right? "The scoring, the assists, the rebounding, the steals, the numbers speak for themselves. But what you don't see at times is the impact off the floor. As a rookie to come in and have the impact that she's had in helping us navigate adversity and tough times and keeping that locker room together and just truly leading by example with a process-oriented approach. "She works so hard to make sure she's ready on game days. That's physically and mentally. And so I'm just happy that, you know, it's everything on the floor is coming together because nobody works harder off the floor." And while she is just a rookie, her play on the court would suggest otherwise, as she continues to show poise beyond her years, averaging 18.8 points, 5.4 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 34 minutes per game, with no moment too bright for the star. For Bueckers, her ability to be a leader both on and off the court is not lost on her, as she told reporters before the game. "I think instilling confidence in my teammates has always been something that I've been confident in," she explained of her leadership style. "Just being able to get the best out of everybody around me. Balancing that with being able to challenge and praise. "Finding the perfect medium of that. Wanting to hold your teammates accountable, hold yourself accountable. But also praising them." And while the star is a vocal leader for the Wings, she made it clear that it was a collaborative effort from her and the rest of the team. In the same vein, the 23-year-old star explained that her biggest personal growth comes from the fact that she just naturally gravitated to being a leader. "I think my voice and my leadership ability," Bueckers continued. "Coming in as a rookie, you just want to gain everybody's respect and not step on toes. "But to be confident in my voice and my teammates and my coaching staff. Helping me build confidence in that and be receptive to it. I feel like I've gone far." Though the Wings are in the midst of a transition season as Dallas continues to find the proper pieces to place around Bueckers, the guard is clearly taking charge as the organization's star for the future. And while fans can see her perform at an elite level every night, it is her impact in all facets of basketball that truly makes her the star that she is.
